title: How much can this process produce?
description: Change a stage's speed to see what limits the whole process and how much output fits in a shift.
assumptions: Every unit passes through all three stages, with one unit leaving each stage for every unit entering it.
Steady flow: enough work and buffering keep the slowest stage supplied. Startup time, downtime, defects and transfer delays are excluded.
Shift output is a theoretical capacity, rounded down to whole units. It is not a delivery promise.

inputs.label: Prepare
inputs.help: How many units the first stage can handle each hour.

inputs.label: Assemble
inputs.help: How many units the second stage can handle each hour.

inputs.label: Pack
inputs.help: How many units the third stage can handle each hour.

inputs.label: Shift length
inputs.help: Available operating hours, after any planned breaks.

inputs.label: Units needed
inputs.help: Compare the theoretical capacity with a target.

outputs.label: Process capacity
outputs.help: The slowest stage limits the whole process. Improving another stage alone does not increase this number.

outputs.label: Possible in this shift
outputs.help: Process capacity × shift hours, rounded down to whole units.

outputs.label: Units short of target
outputs.help: Zero means the stated target fits within this model's capacity.

constraints.message: The target exceeds this shift's theoretical capacity. Increase the limiting stage, extend the shift, or reduce the target.
